alt: Satellite image of the parallel folded ridges of the Appalachian Mountains and Chesapeake Bay.
caption: NASA Terra MODIS, 15 September 2023. Appalachian ridges and valleys across Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland and Pennsylvania preserve the structure of an ancient mountain belt.

alt: A green auroral band glows below the International Space Station above the southern Indian Ocean.
caption: An ISS photograph of aurora north of Antarctica. Energetic particles excite upper-atmosphere gases; the green light is emitted by the atmosphere, not reflected sunlight.

alt: NOAA bathymetry map of the South Atlantic showing continental shelves and the mid-ocean ridge.
caption: NOAA South Atlantic bathymetry. Colour represents seafloor depth, revealing continental margins, abyssal basins and the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

alt: A circular CTD instrument and water-sampling rosette is lowered into the ocean.
caption: NOAA CTD rosette. Conductivity, temperature and pressure measurements describe salinity and density through the water column; bottle samples provide independent checks.

alt: NASA Blue Marble satellite imagery displayed in a Mollweide projection with a graticule.
caption: NASA satellite imagery reprojected by Strebe into Mollweide. This equal-area projection preserves relative areas but distorts shapes; the ocean has been lightened for legibility.

alt: Rounded hills and fields around the Vale of Edale, viewed from Grindslow Knoll.
caption: The Vale of Edale and Lose Hill, Peak District, England. A landscape photograph shows local relief, ridges and valley slopes.

alt: Cyclone Evan's spiral cloud bands cross the islands of Fiji in a NASA satellite image.
caption: Aqua MODIS observed Cyclone Evan near Fiji on 16 December 2012. Its cloud bands spiral around the centre; a mathematical logarithmic spiral is an approximation, not a measured exact fit.

alt: A broad flat river plain with autumn vegetation in the Ahuriri valley, New Zealand.
caption: Ahuriri River plain near Omarama, New Zealand. River deposition builds a relatively flat valley floor between higher ground.

credit: NASA Kennedy Space Center, KSC-00PP-0096 · public domain · via Wikimedia Commons · resized
alt: The Moon appears copper-red during a lunar eclipse viewed from Merritt Island, Florida.
caption: NASA Kennedy Space Center photograph, 20 January 2000. Earth's shadow falls on the Moon; sunlight filtered through Earth's atmosphere gives the eclipsed surface a reddish colour.

alt: Swarm-derived maps compare Earth's magnetic field intensity in 2014 and 2025, with a nanoTesla scale.
caption: Swarm-based core-field models for 2014 and 2025, in nanoTesla. Satellite measurements constrain the field generated mainly by motion of conducting liquid in the outer core; this is not a photograph of the core.

alt: NASA Blue Marble imagery in Mercator projection, with strongly enlarged high-latitude regions.
caption: NASA Blue Marble imagery reprojected by Mdf into Mercator. Local angles are preserved, area grows towards the poles, and a constant-bearing route plots as a straight line.

alt: A small stream runs along a valley much larger than its present channel.
caption: A photographed misfit stream. Its present flow is small relative to its valley; former glacial meltwater or a change in drainage may explain the mismatch.

alt: Voyager 2 image of Neptune's blue disc showing cloud bands and the Great Dark Spot.
caption: NASA/JPL Voyager 2 image assembled from green and orange filter observations in August 1989. Neptune is an ice giant; its displayed deep blue is enhanced relative to its natural appearance.

alt: Water falls through a narrow rocky step into a dark plunge pool at Cwmorthin, Wales.
caption: Cwmorthin waterfall and plunge pool, Wales. Falling water and entrained sediment erode the pool below the step in the river bed.

alt: NASA map of low ozone concentrations over Antarctica in September 2023.
caption: NASA Ozone Watch and GEOS-5, 21 September 2023. The mapped ozone hole is a region of depleted stratospheric ozone; colour represents measured or analysed ozone, not a visible opening.

alt: Rounded grey stones and pebbles of different sizes on an English North Sea beach.
caption: Pebbles on the North Sea coast of England. Repeated collisions can round and reduce fragments through attrition; a still image records the resulting grains.

credit: NASA Blue Marble / Mdf (projection) · public domain · via Wikimedia Commons · resized
alt: NASA Blue Marble satellite imagery displayed in the curved-outline Robinson projection.
caption: NASA satellite imagery in Robinson projection. This compromise projection balances several distortions; it preserves neither all areas nor all local angles.

alt: Tree roots grow into joints in rock beside a roadside exposure.
caption: Roots grow through existing rock joints. Their growth can widen cracks, contributing to biological and physical weathering.

alt: Aquarius satellite map of ocean surface salinity with warm colours in saltier subtropical waters.
caption: NASA Aquarius surface-salinity composite, August–September 2011. Colours show salt concentration; black marks missing data. This early product contains calibration artefacts and is not a map of deep-water salinity.

alt: Multibeam sonar bathymetry reveals a broad undersea mountain in the Arctic Ocean.
caption: NOAA Office of Coast Survey multibeam measurements of an Arctic seamount. The coloured relief is a visualisation of measured seabed shape, not an underwater photograph.

alt: Uneven displaced ground and scarps above the coast at Redcliff Point, Dorset.
caption: Slumping above Redcliff Point, Dorset. Rotational movement displaces blocks along a curved shear surface; the surface scars and tilted ground provide evidence.

alt: A long-exposure photograph of Orion's stars, red emission nebulae and dark dust clouds.
caption: Orion photographed from ESO's La Silla Observatory by Zdeněk Bardon. Stars that appear close in the sky can lie at very different distances; long exposure reveals faint gas and dust.

alt: CERES global map of outgoing longwave radiation with a colour scale in watts per square metre.
caption: NASA CERES, April 2015. Satellite observations map outgoing thermal radiation at the top of the atmosphere in W m⁻²; colder cloud tops generally emit less than warm clear-sky regions.

alt: A sequence of dark Venus silhouettes crosses the Sun in SDO ultraviolet observations.
caption: NASA SDO, 5–6 June 2012. A time sequence of ultraviolet observations shows Venus crossing the solar disc. The repeated silhouettes are different times, not several planets.
